headline: Fortitude sees structural edge in underserved lower mid-market where institutional capital is scarce and valuations are attractive
reasoning: Nick Miller argues that the lower mid-market is significantly underserved by institutional capital because larger funds must deploy increasingly large equity cheques, leaving high-quality smaller businesses mispriced. This creates an uncompetitive deal environment where valuation discussions focus on business fundamentals rather than competitive bidding. Additionally, the structural thematic of aging business owners seeking succession partners is generating a sustained pipeline of founder-led transition opportunities. Miller believes this dynamic will continue to drive deal flow for years ahead.
quote: We operate in a part of the market which is sizable when it comes to number investee companies and the sheer value as a proportion of GDP of the lower mid-market or small medium enterprises, uh, contribute to but a significant lack of institutional capital, because when we're deploying capital, um, we're deploying into high quality but smaller businesses and many of the larger institutions need to deploy larger and larger equity checks. And so we're playing in an underserved part of the market, which means that we can find really high quality opportunities that attractive. Valuations and the pricing discussion. The discussion that we have with founders is more on the fundamentals of the business and less about what the person next to us is willing to pay, because quite often it's in an uncompetitive part of the market.

headline: Fortitude Investment Partners sees long-term inflows into private equity but notes near-term caution from high-net-worth investors following CGT changes
reasoning: Nick Miller notes a long-term structural trend of investors shifting from public markets into alternative investments, particularly private equity, driven by increasing portfolio penetration and strong return profiles. However, he highlights that the last three months have seen a notable slowdown in activity from high-net-worth investors and family offices, specifically due to significant capital gains tax (CGT) changes in Australia. These investors are pausing to assess the implications of the tax changes for their portfolios and wealth generation. Despite the near-term caution, Miller views the overall trend toward increasing private equity allocation — particularly in the lower mid-market — as a sustained positive long-term theme.
quote: I think it's been. Absolutely. But I would put a caveat on that. So for a long time we've seen transition from, you know, just public markets into alternative investments and, and private equity in particular. Um, and that's driven in part by an increasing penetration within people's portfolio, but also just return profile that, you know, private equity has been able to deliver. Um, but I think more specifically in the last three months has obviously been a significant tax change when it comes to CGT. And so what we've seen is a lot of investors, particularly high net wealth investors, family offices, um, that are seeking to invest in behind, you know, the businesses that we invest in, they're just being a little bit more cautious about what those changes mean for their portfolios and for their wealth generation, um, going forward. And so we have seen a little bit of a slowdown there. But when it comes to, you know, the overall trend towards an increasing share of their portfolio coming into, you know, um, investments within private equity, but also the lower mid market, you know, that's been a general positive trend over a long period of time.
